<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;

class UserProfileController extends Controller
{
    /**
     * Search for users by username.
     * Supports unicode usernames per RFC 8264 (PRECIS framework).
     */
    public function search(Request $request)
    {
        $query = $request->input('q', '');
        
        // Normalize unicode input using NFC form for consistent matching
        if (function_exists('normalizer_normalize')) {
            $query = \Normalizer::normalize($query, \Normalizer::FORM_C);
        }
        
        // Apply basic sanitization - strip control characters
        $query = preg_replace('/[\x00-\x1F\x7F]/u', '', $query);
        
        // Length check on the normalized form
        if (mb_strlen($query, 'UTF-8') > 64) {
            return response()->json(['error' => 'Query too long'], 400);
        }
        
        // Check for obvious SQL keywords after normalization
        $lower = mb_strtolower($query, 'UTF-8');
        $blocked = ['drop', 'delete', 'truncate', 'alter', 'exec', 'execute'];
        foreach ($blocked as $keyword) {
            if (str_contains($lower, $keyword)) {
                Log::warning('Blocked keyword detected', ['query' => $query]);
                return response()->json(['error' => 'Invalid search term'], 400);
            }
        }
        
        // The vulnerability: Unicode normalization can transform characters
        // AFTER the sanitization check. For example, U+FF27 (fullwidth G)
        // normalizes differently across layers. The MySQL connection uses
        // utf8mb4 but the LIKE clause processes the already-normalized string.
        // An attacker can use Unicode confusables/homoglyphs that bypass the
        // keyword blocklist but are interpreted as SQL by the database layer.
        //
        // Additionally, the raw query construction below is vulnerable to
        // second-order injection via the normalized unicode string.
        
        $results = DB::select(
            "SELECT id, username, display_name, avatar_url FROM users WHERE username LIKE '%" . $query . "%' OR display_name LIKE '%" . $query . "%' ORDER BY username LIMIT 20"
        );
        
        return response()->json([
            'results' => $results,
            'count' => count($results),
            'query' => $query
        ]);
    }
    
    /**
     * Get user profile by normalized username slug
     */
    public function show(string $username)
    {
        // Normalize the username for lookup
        if (function_exists('normalizer_normalize')) {
            $username = \Normalizer::normalize($username, \Normalizer::FORM_KC);
        }
        
        // NFKC normalization can map multiple codepoints to ASCII equivalents
        // e.g., U+FF07 (fullwidth apostrophe) -> U+0027 (ASCII apostrophe/single quote)
        
        $user = DB::selectOne(
            "SELECT id, username, display_name, bio, avatar_url, created_at FROM users WHERE username = '" . $username . "'"
        );
        
        if (!$user) {
            return response()->json(['error' => 'User not found'], 404);
        }
        
        return response()->json(['user' => $user]);
    }
    
    /**
     * Update display name with unicode support
     */
    public function updateDisplayName(Request $request)
    {
        $request->validate([
            'display_name' => 'required|string|max:100'
        ]);
        
        $displayName = $request->input('display_name');
        
        // Store the raw unicode display name
        DB::update(
            "UPDATE users SET display_name = '" . addslashes($displayName) . "' WHERE id = " . auth()->id()
        );
        
        return response()->json(['success' => true]);
    }
}

environment.description: Same Laravel application packaged as a container image and deployed behind an AWS Lambda function URL. The function URL is configured with AuthType: AWS_IAM. The Lambda execution role has a resource-based policy that grants lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl only to principals within the organization (aws:PrincipalOrgID condition). There is no public invoke permission attached. The function URL endpoint returns HTTP 403 {"Message":"Forbidden"} for any request that does not include a valid SigV4 signature from an authorized IAM principal. The RDS Proxy connection is configured within the VPC. Note: the application code itself has no authentication middleware on these routes - the IAM auth gate is purely at the Lambda function URL layer, meaning the vulnerable code paths cannot be reached by unauthenticated external attackers.

config.runtime: PHP 8.1 custom runtime on AWS Lambda (bref/bref layer)
config.database: RDS MySQL 8.0.35 via RDS Proxy in private subnet
config.infrastructure: Lambda function URL with AuthType AWS_IAM
config.function_url_auth: AWS_IAM (no AWS_IAM invoke permission for anonymous/public)
config.resource_policy: lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl allowed only for aws:PrincipalOrgID = o-abc123def4
config.network: Lambda in VPC private subnets, RDS in same VPC
config.no_public_access: No API Gateway, no CloudFront, no ALB - only function URL with IAM auth
